head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Rebuild reachability in collective combiners only after a combine.

The combiners rebuilt the reachability map and the post order for every group
they looked at, even when the group had one instruction and nothing changed.
They now rebuild only after instructions were actually combined. Results are
unchanged; the passes are faster on modules with many collectives.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model occupancy for single-reduce fusion estimates

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model occupancy for single-reduce fusion estimates

We are reusing the occupancy function in the dot cost model as it doesn't have operation specific logic and can be used here.

`GpuPerformanceModelWithIndexingAnalysis` assumes that the compute and memory
access time of a tiled fusion overlap almost fully, whatever the tile size.
Blocks are not pipelined, so the compute of a block only overlaps with the
memory accesses of the other blocks resident on the same core.

We should expand the occupancy measure beyond reductions. I only have evidence that it helps reductions, and generalizing this needs to be validated first. I'd rather do this incrementally.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

Adds `GpuCommunicator::AcquireSymmetricMemory` and `ReleaseSymmetricMemory`. `AcquireSymmetricMemory` returns a shared registration that stays cached on the communicator until `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` is called for the same address or the communicator is destroyed or aborted. The default implementation falls back to an uncached `CreateSymmetricMemory`.

This cache is not used yet it will be needed later to move NCCL window registration from executable level to the NCCL communicator level.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

Pruning was wasteful as a strategy as it still hits the compile-time due to trying many configurations that aren't useful. Instead, the microbenchmarks were analyzed to see where we improve with tiling reduction dimensions. This change uses an opt-in strategy instead.

The most impactful cases were shown to be column reductions. For these cases tiling the reduce dimension allows us to use bigger tiles for minor parallel dimensions that can benefit from coalescing. The thresholds used are empirical from the data, but they look reasonable.

The change only applies behind flags, so production is unaffected. Follow-up changes will modify the cost model to improve the top-1 candidates and enable tiled reductions for kernels with no more than one reduce op.

head_commit.message:
PR #53203: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53203

📝 Summary of Changes

Let `MoveCopyToUsers` move a `copy` that produces an element of the initial state of a `while` loop into the body of the loop.

When a consumer of a slice requires a particular layout, layout assignment gives that layout to the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop. `MoveCopyToUsers` already turns `slice(copy(x))` into `copy(slice(x))`, but it did not see this copy, because the copy and the slice are in different computations.

With this change the copy is moved into the body if:

- the body passes the element on unchanged, nothing in the body reads the state the body returns, and the element is not read in the condition,
- apart from that, the element is only read as the operand of `slice` or `dynamic-slice`, in the body and after the loop,
- the slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not larger than twice the element. If the body slices the element, the trip count has to be known.

The bound is twice the element and not the element, because the copy of a slice can be fused with the slice, and copying somewhat more is accepted for not keeping the element in two layouts.

The loop then carries the element in the layout it has before the copy. Each slice, in the body or after the loop, reads a copy of the element, and the existing rewrite moves that copy below the slice.

**Before:** the whole array is copied before the loop.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  copy = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(weights)
  init = tuple(zero, copy, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

**After:** only the slice is copied.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  slice = f32[1,16,32]{2,1,0} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(slice)
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  init = tuple(zero, weights, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

🎯 Justification

Training workloads store weights as large stacks and process one layer at a time inside a loop. Copying the whole stack for the layout of a per-layer collective keeps a second copy of the stack alive while the loop runs.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement (GPU memory)

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Layout assignment gives the layout required by a consumer of a slice to
the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced
array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop, although
MoveCopyToUsers could move the copy below the slice if both were in the
same computation.

Let MoveCopyToUsers move a copy that produces an element of the initial
state of a while loop into the body of the loop, if the body passes the
element on unchanged, only reads slices of it, and the slices of all
iterations together are not larger than the element. The loop then
carries the element in the layout it has before the copy, and only the
slices are copied.

Also run MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter, which
only rewrites an all-gather whose operand is a copy.

--
04668b01c19c19e38d3461897cfd8313630c12dc by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy into a while body that is also sliced after the loop

A loop that is unrolled with double buffering reads the last layers of a
stack after the loop, and its body slices the stack several times per
iteration. The copy of such a stack was not moved into the body.

Give the slices of the element after the loop a copy of the element as
well, like the slices in the body, and limit what each slice in the body
copies over all iterations instead of the sum of all slices.

8bcb0c57280f3f475823d83da911e834288b15d3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep MoveCopyToUsers out of the layout assignment pipeline

Running MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter can sink the
copy that follows an all-gather below its user. The rewriter only matches
copy -> all-gather -> copy, so it would stop rewriting such an all-gather.

The copy of while loop state is still moved into the loop body by the
MoveCopyToUsers run before LayoutNormalization.

[XLA:GPU] Bound the slices copied for a copy moved into a while body

Move the copy of an element of while loop state into the body only if the
slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not
larger than twice the element. The bound used to be the element, applied to
the largest slice in the body only, and did not count slices after the loop.

--

[XLA:GPU] Do not move a copy into a while body that reads the state it returns

A get-tuple-element of the root of the body would get the layout of the
copied array, while its users expect the layout of the copy.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the trip count is unknown, and that
the trip count is taken from the backend config of the loop.

--

[XLA:GPU] Test moving a copy that has another user into a while body

The copy is still moved into the body, and is kept for its other user.

[XLA:GPU] Wrap a comment in move_copy_to_users.cc at 80 columns

--

[XLA:GPU] Avoid an overflow when bounding the slices of a while body

Compare the trip count with the bound before multiplying it with the size of
the slices of one iteration, so that a large trip count does not overflow and
pass the bound.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the condition reads the element or if

Only move copies that change the dimension order alone, not copies to
another memory space, to a packed layout or of dynamic shapes. Reject a
negative known trip count. Drop control dependencies and check that the
copy is unused before removing it.

d1b62117da18448b34af9c8e163afc0dc954eef3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Layout assignment gives the layout required by a consumer of a slice to
the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced
array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop, although
MoveCopyToUsers could move the copy below the slice if both were in the
same computation.

Let MoveCopyToUsers move a copy that produces an element of the initial
state of a while loop into the body of the loop, if the body passes the
element on unchanged, only reads slices of it, and the slices of all
iterations together are not larger than the element. The loop then
carries the element in the layout it has before the copy, and only the
slices are copied.

Also run MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter, which
only rewrites an all-gather whose operand is a copy.

--
04668b01c19c19e38d3461897cfd8313630c12dc by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy into a while body that is also sliced after the loop

A loop that is unrolled with double buffering reads the last layers of a
stack after the loop, and its body slices the stack several times per
iteration. The copy of such a stack was not moved into the body.

Give the slices of the element after the loop a copy of the element as
well, like the slices in the body, and limit what each slice in the body
copies over all iterations instead of the sum of all slices.

--
8bcb0c57280f3f475823d83da911e834288b15d3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep MoveCopyToUsers out of the layout assignment pipeline

Running MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter can sink the
copy that follows an all-gather below its user. The rewriter only matches
copy -> all-gather -> copy, so it would stop rewriting such an all-gather.

The copy of while loop state is still moved into the loop body by the
MoveCopyToUsers run before LayoutNormalization.

--
b3766807c7c7a6f4ee0ebd023d6178c699d31f75 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Bound the slices copied for a copy moved into a while body

Move the copy of an element of while loop state into the body only if the
slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not
larger than twice the element. The bound used to be the element, applied to
the largest slice in the body only, and did not count slices after the loop.

--
972363c6f39dd6df1f626494f1f53ad1d1113632 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Do not move a copy into a while body that reads the state it returns

A get-tuple-element of the root of the body would get the layout of the
copied array, while its users expect the layout of the copy.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the trip count is unknown, and that
the trip count is taken from the backend config of the loop.

ca5c93551fbfc81fe448351aa43a3b32ec1fd00a by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Test moving a copy that has another user into a while body

The copy is still moved into the body, and is kept for its other user.

Compare the trip count with the bound before multiplying it with the size of

display_title: PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.

e7e813477d5b08386aaf577217b60473aa2a60aa by Keshav <keshavb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

A call annotated with _xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>" is
wrapped into an async region by ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper and
assigned LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>) by ExecutionStreamAssignment, so it
runs on that domain's stream. The wrapper rejects locality-domain regions
that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and
AsyncStartThunk::Prepare rejects communication thunks inside them at
runtime. Stream annotations are kept only on the call, not on the
get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.

Merging this change closes #52821

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the parent keeps the child-handle storage alive until it is torn down. `PollUntilDone` now reports a failed `ncclCommGetAsyncError` query separately from an async operation error.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

16ca7fc76dcb82c380e800cad86aaf902849ecac by Jane Liu <janeliu@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Make NCCL communicator teardown safe for late child cleanup.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Make NCCL communicator teardown safe for late child cleanup.

Calling NCCL cleanup functions on a destroyed or aborted `ncclComm_t` handle is undefined behavior. This happens when a symmetric memory window, registered buffer, or device communicator outlives an aborted or destroyed `NcclCommunicator`, such as with communicator-level window caching.

`NcclCommunicator` now clears `comm_->comm` and resets `num_symmetric_windows` right before calling `ncclCommDestroy` or `ncclCommAbort`. `NcclSymmetricMemory`, `NcclRegisteredMemory`, and `NcclDeviceCommunicator` destructors check for a null communicator handle and skip `ncclCommWindowDeregister`, `ncclCommDeregister`, and `ncclDevCommDestroy` when the parent communicator is gone.

In `dot_handler.cc`, `UpdateDDNums` updated `DotDimensionNumbers` for bidirectional `EmitWindowedDotGeneral` by appending `reshaped_dim` and sorting by dimension index, assuming contracting and batch dimensions were sorted. XLA pairs `lhs` and `rhs` contracting and batch dimensions by list position, so nonascending dimension lists silently mispaired axes when shard sizes matched. Record the original list index of `reshaped_dim` before shifting dimensions, and insert `reshaped_dim` at that position instead of sorting.

head_commit.message:
PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation. The runtime version is necessary but not sufficient — the kernel driver, the container or the device may still refuse fd export — so a rejected granularity query or hipMemCreate() falls back to hipMemHandleTypeNone with a warning, as the CUDA allocator does. Workloads that never export keep running.

🎯 Justification

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: ✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests: Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both directions, the fallback leaving allocation intact, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer from the kVmm allocator.

[XLA:GPU] Support dots with downstream transposes in indexing cost model.

Move the downstream `kTranspose` rejection out of

display_title: [XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

📝 Summary of Changes

HloRematerialization's host-offload strategy picks a candidate from the buffer-level user list (GetUsers, every position of the value), but OffloadInstruction places the copy back to device before the first unplaced user in the instruction's own users(). The two lists differ when the value is also read through another instruction's output, for example forwarded into an async-start's output tuple and read by the async-done. If the only direct user (the async-start) is already placed, OffloadInstruction finds nothing and CHECK-fails: "Have nothing to place this before!".

GetCostOfHostOffload now rejects candidates whose buffer has indirect uses. This is conservative: OffloadInstruction only rewires direct users, and the memory tracker would hand the indirect users to the new copy and count the original buffer as free while a placed async-start still holds it. ExtendRecomputeBlock already skips such buffers for recompute because liveness is hard to reason about.

Compression is not changed. It cannot hit this CHECK (it needs an unplaced direct user), but AddCompressInstructions has the same accounting problem when a placed async-start coexists with an unplaced direct user. That deserves its own change and test.

🎯 Justification

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51432. The module from the issue aborts GPU compilation at head (hlo-opt --platform=gpu --stage=hlo-backend, a100_sxm_80 target spec, --xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading=true). With this change it compiles.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in hlo_rematerialization_test.cc. SkipOffloadWhenOnlyUserIsAsyncStart: the only user of an add is an already placed async-start; without the fix it aborts on the CHECK. SkipOffloadWhenAsyncStartIsPlacedBeforeDirectUser: the add also has a later direct user; without the fix it is offloaded anyway and the tracker reports a 4 KiB saving while the async-start still holds the buffer. With the fix both leave the add alone and offload the next candidate.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

head_commit.message:
PR #52896: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52896

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`ConvolutionThunk` requires a warmup: a command buffer that holds a convolution runs once on each device without recording and is captured from its second execution. This is the mechanism custom calls and collectives already use.

## 🎯 Justification

With `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=+CONVOLUTION`, a convolution's first execution is recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there, which fails on both vendors:

- **ROCm:** creating the MIOpen handle calls `hipMalloc` (through hipBLASLt), which is not allowed while capturing, so the capture is invalidated (`hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`).
- **CUDA:** creating the cuDNN handle fails inside the capture. When the executable comes from the compilation cache, the cuDNN plan is also finalized inside the capture and the launch fails (`CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`).

This hits every GPU except the one that ran autotuning, and a single GPU when the executable is loaded from a compilation cache. The warmup execution does this setup outside any capture; the runner is cached per device, so the recorded execution only launches it.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`command_buffer_conversion_pass_test`: the convolution in a converted command buffer requires a warmup. The warmup itself is covered by `command_buffer_thunk_test`.

display_title: Move ORC object loading out of `CpuAotLoader` behind `RegisterObjectFileLoader`

head_commit.message:
Move ORC object loading out of `CpuAotLoader` behind `RegisterObjectFileLoader`

AOT runtimes shouldn't link ORC (and with it most of LLVM) just to load the kernels of a precompiled artifact.

So the ORC code moves to `:cpu_aot_object_file_loader`, which registers itself at static init and is linked by `cpu_compiler_pure`. The compiler and every runtime that links it keep loading object files with ORC exactly as before, and `CpuAotLoader` returns FailedPrecondition when no loader is registered. A `check_deps` target keeps ORC out of `:cpu_aot_loader`. `nanort_executable` (used by Lite AOT and other runtimes that don't link the compiler) links the ORC registration explicitly, so their behavior doesn't change either.

This is the `RegisterObjectFileLoader` part of cl/999191401, without the `LiteObjectLoader` fallback (and its diffbases), since the shared object loader will take that role in a later change.

unchanged; the passes are faster on modules with many collectives.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model concat loop copies, shared-memory limit and prologue compute in dot fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model concat loop copies, shared-memory limit and prologue compute in dot fusions.

As part of migrating `gpu_dot_fusion_cost_model` into
`GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`, account for three Triton mainloop behaviors that
were previously ignored:

- `kConcatenate` inside the K-loop unswitches the loop across its branches
  without aliasing shared-memory buffers, multiplying shared-memory usage when
  pipelined (`num_stages > 1`).
- Configs whose per-block shared memory exceeds the hardware opt-in limit fail
  Triton compilation and now return infinite runtime.
- SIMT prologue FLOPs in the dot region run inside the K-loop (overlapped with
  async MMA on Hopper+, or serialized with `mma.sync` on older GPUs).

head_commit.message:
PR #53288: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI]: Fix oneAPI post-submit build failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53288

[0cae2f6](https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/0cae2f62026e1ab16ad5f78097ceccba64474853) commit in XLA caused the oneAPI postsubmit to fail with the following error:
```
xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc:1404:20: error: no matching member function for call to 'emplace'
 1404 |     stream_options.emplace();
      |     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~
external/rules_ml_toolchain++toolchain_ext+sysroot_linux_x86_64_glibc_2_31/usr/include/c++/10/optional:847:2: note: candidate template ignored: requirement 'is_constructible_v<xla::LocalDeviceState::StreamOptions>' was not satisfied [with _Args = <>]
  847 |         emplace(_Args&&... __args)
      |         ^
external/rules_ml_toolchain++toolchain_ext+sysroot_linux_x86_64_glibc_2_31/usr/include/c++/10/optional:857:2: note: candidate function template not viable: requires at least argument '__il', but no arguments were provided
  857 |         emplace(initializer_list<_Up> __il, _Args&&... __args)
      |         ^       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
```
This PR fixes the error by initializing `StreamOptions` using designated initializers since Clang with GCC-10 libstdc++ rejects the no-argument `emplace()` which is a known [LLVM bug #50248](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/50248).
Copybara import of the project:

Fix oneAPI build failure by initializing `StreamOptions` with designated initializers instead of a no-argument emplace().

Merging this change closes #53288

display_title: Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

head_commit.message:
Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

The table of host functions that XLA:CPU kernels can call (libm, fp16 and bf16 conversions, `__powisf2`, ...) lives inside `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator`, which is an ORC definition generator, so loaders that don't use ORC can't reuse it.

So we move the table to `:builtin_symbols` (`FindBuiltinSymbol`), which doesn't depend on LLVM, and `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator` looks names up there. That way ORC and `LiteObjectLoader` (next CLs) resolve exactly the same symbols.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 999190832

display_title: PR #53203: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

head_commit.message:
PR #53203: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53203

📝 Summary of Changes

Let `MoveCopyToUsers` move a `copy` that produces an element of the initial state of a `while` loop into the body of the loop.

When a consumer of a slice requires a particular layout, layout assignment gives that layout to the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop. `MoveCopyToUsers` already turns `slice(copy(x))` into `copy(slice(x))`, but it did not see this copy, because the copy and the slice are in different computations.

With this change the copy is moved into the body if:

- the body passes the element on unchanged, nothing in the body reads the state the body returns, and the element is not read in the condition,
- apart from that, the element is only read as the operand of `slice` or `dynamic-slice`, in the body and after the loop,
- the slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not larger than twice the element. If the body slices the element, the trip count has to be known.

The bound is twice the element and not the element, because the copy of a slice can be fused with the slice, and copying somewhat more is accepted for not keeping the element in two layouts.

The loop then carries the element in the layout it has before the copy. Each slice, in the body or after the loop, reads a copy of the element, and the existing rewrite moves that copy below the slice.

**Before:** the whole array is copied before the loop.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  copy = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(weights)
  init = tuple(zero, copy, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

**After:** only the slice is copied.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  slice = f32[1,16,32]{2,1,0} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(slice)
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  init = tuple(zero, weights, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

🎯 Justification

Training workloads store weights as large stacks and process one layer at a time inside a loop. Copying the whole stack for the layout of a per-layer collective keeps a second copy of the stack alive while the loop runs.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement (GPU memory)

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

MaxText training on NVIDIA GB300, 5 runs per variant, base and new interleaved on the same node(s). Measured at commit 04668b01c1 of this branch, before the bound on the slices was changed; to be repeated at the head of the branch.

- a copy is moved into a while body that only reads slices of the element, in the body and after the loop,
- the copy is not moved if the slices exceed the bound, if the trip count is unknown, or if the loop reads or changes the element in any other way.

d1b62117da18448b34af9c8e163afc0dc954eef3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Layout assignment gives the layout required by a consumer of a slice to
the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced
array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop, although
MoveCopyToUsers could move the copy below the slice if both were in the
same computation.

Let MoveCopyToUsers move a copy that produces an element of the initial
state of a while loop into the body of the loop, if the body passes the
element on unchanged, only reads slices of it, and the slices of all
iterations together are not larger than the element. The loop then
carries the element in the layout it has before the copy, and only the
slices are copied.

Also run MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter, which
only rewrites an all-gather whose operand is a copy.

--
04668b01c19c19e38d3461897cfd8313630c12dc by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy into a while body that is also sliced after the loop

A loop that is unrolled with double buffering reads the last layers of a
stack after the loop, and its body slices the stack several times per
iteration. The copy of such a stack was not moved into the body.

Give the slices of the element after the loop a copy of the element as
well, like the slices in the body, and limit what each slice in the body
copies over all iterations instead of the sum of all slices.

--
8bcb0c57280f3f475823d83da911e834288b15d3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep MoveCopyToUsers out of the layout assignment pipeline

Running MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter can sink the
copy that follows an all-gather below its user. The rewriter only matches
copy -> all-gather -> copy, so it would stop rewriting such an all-gather.

The copy of while loop state is still moved into the loop body by the
MoveCopyToUsers run before LayoutNormalization.

--
b3766807c7c7a6f4ee0ebd023d6178c699d31f75 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Bound the slices copied for a copy moved into a while body

Move the copy of an element of while loop state into the body only if the
slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not
larger than twice the element. The bound used to be the element, applied to
the largest slice in the body only, and did not count slices after the loop.

--
972363c6f39dd6df1f626494f1f53ad1d1113632 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Do not move a copy into a while body that reads the state it returns

A get-tuple-element of the root of the body would get the layout of the
copied array, while its users expect the layout of the copy.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the trip count is unknown, and that
the trip count is taken from the backend config of the loop.

--
ca5c93551fbfc81fe448351aa43a3b32ec1fd00a by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Test moving a copy that has another user into a while body

The copy is still moved into the body, and is kept for its other user.

--
7d8bf51c962e52cfb5732b32b6b52d56f881b2a1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Wrap a comment in move_copy_to_users.cc at 80 columns

--
c39135eb5f777232926fc615c0e436ca5eb3d717 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Avoid an overflow when bounding the slices of a while body

Compare the trip count with the bound before multiplying it with the size of
the slices of one iteration, so that a large trip count does not overflow and
pass the bound.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the condition reads the element or if
the body is called by two loops, spell out a StatusOr type, and mention the
size bound in the header comment.

--
5e7cf1f0da5ba3ba17d9007e1b3b200d892a098e by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Format move_copy_to_users.cc

--
9424fb2c229251c608655332bdd26d58f5a3d6c5 by Shawn Wang (Compute Arch) <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Harden MoveCopyToUsers while-body copy matching

Only move copies that change the dimension order alone, not copies to
another memory space, to a packed layout or of dynamic shapes. Reject a
negative known trip count. Drop control dependencies and check that the
copy is unused before removing it.

Merging this change closes #53203

display_title: [XLA] Rebuild reachability in collective combiners only after a combine.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Rebuild reachability in collective combiners only after a combine.

The combiners rebuilt the reachability map and the post order for every group
they looked at, even when the group had one instruction and nothing changed.
They now rebuild only after instructions were actually combined. Results are
unchanged; the passes are faster on modules with many collectives.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix sub-byte operand read bytes and batched dot shared-memory sizing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix sub-byte operand read bytes and batched dot shared-memory sizing.

Fusion operand read estimation previously rounded each element up to whole
bytes, overcounting tiled read bytes and L2 read traffic by 2x on bit-packed
4-bit quantized operands (assuming sub-byte operands are packed in memory).
Meanwhile, per-block dot shared-memory sizing omitted the batch tile multiplier
(`b > 1`), truncated odd bit totals via floor division by 8, and sized `pred`
tiles at 1 bit instead of 8-bit storage width.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Preserve dot dimension order in UpdateDDNums

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Preserve dot dimension order in UpdateDDNums

In `dot_handler.cc`, `UpdateDDNums` updated `DotDimensionNumbers` for bidirectional `EmitWindowedDotGeneral` by appending `reshaped_dim` and sorting by dimension index, assuming contracting and batch dimensions were sorted. XLA pairs `lhs` and `rhs` contracting and batch dimensions by list position, so nonascending dimension lists silently mispaired axes when shard sizes matched. Record the original list index of `reshaped_dim` before shifting dimensions, and insert `reshaped_dim` at that position instead of sorting.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021389370

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support native MLIR kInput, multi-output, and DAG stages in MultiPhaseFusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support native MLIR kInput, multi-output, and DAG stages in MultiPhaseFusion.

`ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` can now lower `kReduction`, `kTranspose`, and `kConcatenate` sub-kernels with any rank, shared memory reuse, partial-CTA barriers, tuple output unpacking, and arbitrary phase DAGs ordered topologically.

Delegate stage eligibility and launch-dimension queries in `MultiPhaseFusion` to `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion::CreateNativeNestedEmitter` (exempting `kLoop` and `kConcatenate` sub-kernels from the warp-multiple thread guard), wrap unfused instructions using `FusionWrapper::ChooseFusionKind`, unpack/rewire multi-output tuple stages via `get-tuple-element`, and generalize subgraph discovery from straight-line chains to connected DAGs while capping total fused kernel arguments (deduplicated external operands plus leaf outputs) at 256.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass kept the unit dimension of a tt.reduce over a [1, N]
row tile, as the result Triton converted the whole row between layouts through
shared memory. Rewrite such reduces as a 1D reduce plus tt.splat.
This cuts MI350X kernel time by up to 33% (softmax) and 15% (RMSNorm), and
lets 1x32768 tiles with 16 warps compile on MI200/MI300 - avoid error:
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Shared memory size limit exceeded.

display_title: [XLA] Use typed steps in ShapeTracker and add a generic Append.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use typed steps in ShapeTracker and add a generic Append.

`ShapeTracker::Step` is now a `std::variant<Reshape, Transpose, Broadcast,
Reduce>` of typed structs instead of one struct whose fields meant different
things depending on its type. `Append(const Step&)` applies any step.

The `Prepend*` methods now share one private implementation that inverts the
tracker, appends the inverse of the step and inverts back. Invalid `Prepend*`
calls now fail without changing the tracker; otherwise there is no behavior
change.

This prepares for slice and pad steps.

display_title: [PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

head_commit.message:
[PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

`xla::HloSharding` permits tuple shardings and sparse nonnegative explicit
device IDs (`device >= num_devices`), neither of which is valid for
`ifrt::HloShardingSpec` or `ifrt::HloSharding` (where explicit tiled device IDs
index `[0, num_shards)`). In addition, `Unknown` shardings are accepted at
construction, but hit `CHECK` failures instead of returning an error in
`IndexDomains`, `UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

Reject tuple `xla::HloSharding`s and explicit tiled device IDs outside
`[0, num_shards)` in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, and return
`InvalidArgumentError` for `Unknown` shardings in `IndexDomains`,
`UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

display_title: PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

head_commit.message:
PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation. The runtime version is necessary but not sufficient — the kernel driver, the container or the device may still refuse fd export — so a rejected granularity query or hipMemCreate() falls back to hipMemHandleTypeNone with a warning, as the CUDA allocator does. Workloads that never export keep running.

🎯 Justification

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: ✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests: Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both directions, the fallback leaving allocation intact, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer from the kVmm allocator.

Copybara import of the project:

display_title: PR #52896: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

head_commit.message:
PR #52896: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52896

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`ConvolutionThunk` requires a warmup: a command buffer that holds a convolution runs once on each device without recording and is captured from its second execution. This is the mechanism custom calls and collectives already use.

## 🎯 Justification

With `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=+CONVOLUTION`, a convolution's first execution is recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there, which fails on both vendors:

- **ROCm:** creating the MIOpen handle calls `hipMalloc` (through hipBLASLt), which is not allowed while capturing, so the capture is invalidated (`hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`).
- **CUDA:** creating the cuDNN handle fails inside the capture. When the executable comes from the compilation cache, the cuDNN plan is also finalized inside the capture and the launch fails (`CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`).

This hits every GPU except the one that ran autotuning, and a single GPU when the executable is loaded from a compilation cache. The warmup execution does this setup outside any capture; the runner is cached per device, so the recorded execution only launches it.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`command_buffer_conversion_pass_test`: the convolution in a converted command buffer requires a warmup. The warmup itself is covered by `command_buffer_thunk_test`.
Copybara import of the project:

--
e4293ecef0eb74e4acf0fa8977cb22ed7c735195 by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

With CONVOLUTION in command buffers, a convolution's first execution is
recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there: the
DNN handle, the runner and, on CUDA, the cuDNN execution plan. That
setup fails inside a capture. Make ConvolutionThunk require a warmup, as
custom calls do, so a command buffer holding a convolution runs once on
each device without recording before it is captured.

595ee3a063cfbbefcd7413bc8e3e4541d8efe89e by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] [CUDA] Check requires_warmup of all converted commands

- ConvertConvolutionAndGemmThunks also puts a fusion (KernelThunk) in
  the command buffer.
- Each command's requires_warmup() is checked against a static table
  keyed by Thunk::Kind: copy, kernel and cuBLASLt matmul do not require
  a warmup, convolution does. A command kind missing from the table
  fails the test.

Merging this change closes #52896

display_title: PR #53203: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

head_commit.message:
PR #53203: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53203

📝 Summary of Changes

Let `MoveCopyToUsers` move a `copy` that produces an element of the initial state of a `while` loop into the body of the loop.

When a consumer of a slice requires a particular layout, layout assignment gives that layout to the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop. `MoveCopyToUsers` already turns `slice(copy(x))` into `copy(slice(x))`, but it did not see this copy, because the copy and the slice are in different computations.

With this change the copy is moved into the body if:

- the body passes the element on unchanged, nothing in the body reads the state the body returns, and the element is not read in the condition,
- apart from that, the element is only read as the operand of `slice` or `dynamic-slice`, in the body and after the loop,
- the slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not larger than twice the element. If the body slices the element, the trip count has to be known.

The bound is twice the element and not the element, because the copy of a slice can be fused with the slice, and copying somewhat more is accepted for not keeping the element in two layouts.

The loop then carries the element in the layout it has before the copy. Each slice, in the body or after the loop, reads a copy of the element, and the existing rewrite moves that copy below the slice.

**Before:** the whole array is copied before the loop.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  copy = f32[8,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(weights)
  init = tuple(zero, copy, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

**After:** only the slice is copied.

```hlo
body {
  stack = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} get-tuple-element(p), index=1
  slice = f32[1,16,32]{2,1,0} dynamic-slice(stack, i, zero, zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={1,16,32}
  layer = f32[1,16,32]{1,0,2} copy(slice)
}
ENTRY main {
  weights = f32[8,16,32]{2,1,0} parameter(0)
  init = tuple(zero, weights, acc)
  loop = while(init), condition=condition, body=body
}
```

🎯 Justification

Training workloads store weights as large stacks and process one layer at a time inside a loop. Copying the whole stack for the layout of a per-layer collective keeps a second copy of the stack alive while the loop runs.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement (GPU memory)

d1b62117da18448b34af9c8e163afc0dc954eef3 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

Layout assignment gives the layout required by a consumer of a slice to
the sliced array. If the slice is inside a while loop and the sliced
array is loop state, the whole array is copied before the loop, although
MoveCopyToUsers could move the copy below the slice if both were in the
same computation.

Let MoveCopyToUsers move a copy that produces an element of the initial
state of a while loop into the body of the loop, if the body passes the
element on unchanged, only reads slices of it, and the slices of all
iterations together are not larger than the element. The loop then
carries the element in the layout it has before the copy, and only the
slices are copied.

Also run MoveCopyToUsers before AllGatherMajorDimensionRewriter, which
only rewrites an all-gather whose operand is a copy.

--
04668b01c19c19e38d3461897cfd8313630c12dc by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Move a copy into a while body that is also sliced after the loop

A loop that is unrolled with double buffering reads the last layers of a
stack after the loop, and its body slices the stack several times per
iteration. The copy of such a stack was not moved into the body.

Give the slices of the element after the loop a copy of the element as
well, like the slices in the body, and limit what each slice in the body
copies over all iterations instead of the sum of all slices.

copy that follows an all-gather below its user. The rewriter only matches
copy -> all-gather -> copy, so it would stop rewriting such an all-gather.

The copy of while loop state is still moved into the loop body by the

Move the copy of an element of while loop state into the body only if the
slices of all iterations and the slices after the loop together are not
larger than twice the element. The bound used to be the element, applied to
the largest slice in the body only, and did not count slices after the loop.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the trip count is unknown, and that
the trip count is taken from the backend config of the loop.

Compare the trip count with the bound before multiplying it with the size of
the slices of one iteration, so that a large trip count does not overflow and
pass the bound.

Also test that the copy is not moved if the condition reads the element or if
the body is called by two loops, spell out a StatusOr type, and mention the
size bound in the header comment.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model concat loop copies, shared-memory limit and prologue compute in dot fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model concat loop copies, shared-memory limit and prologue compute in dot fusions.

As part of migrating `gpu_dot_fusion_cost_model` into
`GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`, account for three Triton mainloop behaviors that
were previously ignored:

- `kConcatenate` inside the K-loop unswitches the loop across its branches
  without aliasing shared-memory buffers, multiplying shared-memory usage when
  pipelined (`num_stages > 1`).
- Configs whose per-block shared memory exceeds the hardware opt-in limit fail
  Triton compilation and now return infinite runtime.
- SIMT prologue FLOPs in the dot region run inside the K-loop (overlapped with
  async MMA on Hopper+, or serialized with `mma.sync` on older GPUs).

display_title: [XLA:SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for EighTpu custom call

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for EighTpu custom call

In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, custom call target `@EighTpu` had no registered `OpShardingRuleAttr` and returned an empty attribute. During Shardy global to local partitioning, `InsertExplicitReshardsPass` skips operations without a sharding rule and `ConvertGlobalToLocalPass` localizes sharded quadrant operands without an `all_gather`, executing independent eigensolvers on disjoint device slices and producing wrong eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Register a sharding rule for validated static square `@EighTpu` calls that propagates leading batch dimensions pointwise and marks the trailing quadrant and eigenvalue dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication`.

head_commit.message:
[PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

`xla::HloSharding` permits tuple shardings and sparse nonnegative explicit
device IDs (`device >= num_devices`), neither of which is valid for
`ifrt::HloShardingSpec` or `ifrt::HloSharding` (where explicit tiled device IDs
index `[0, num_shards)`). In addition, `Unknown` shardings are accepted at
construction, but hit `CHECK` failures instead of returning an error in
`IndexDomains`, `UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

Reject tuple `xla::HloSharding`s and explicit tiled device IDs outside
`[0, num_shards)` in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, and return
`InvalidArgumentError` for `Unknown` shardings in `IndexDomains`,
`UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

display_title: PR #52896: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

head_commit.message:
PR #52896: [ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52896

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`ConvolutionThunk` requires a warmup: a command buffer that holds a convolution runs once on each device without recording and is captured from its second execution. This is the mechanism custom calls and collectives already use.

## 🎯 Justification

With `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=+CONVOLUTION`, a convolution's first execution is recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there, which fails on both vendors:

- **ROCm:** creating the MIOpen handle calls `hipMalloc` (through hipBLASLt), which is not allowed while capturing, so the capture is invalidated (`hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`).
- **CUDA:** creating the cuDNN handle fails inside the capture. When the executable comes from the compilation cache, the cuDNN plan is also finalized inside the capture and the launch fails (`CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`).

This hits every GPU except the one that ran autotuning, and a single GPU when the executable is loaded from a compilation cache. The warmup execution does this setup outside any capture; the runner is cached per device, so the recorded execution only launches it.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`command_buffer_conversion_pass_test`: the convolution in a converted command buffer requires a warmup. The warmup itself is covered by `command_buffer_thunk_test`.
Copybara import of the project:

--
e4293ecef0eb74e4acf0fa8977cb22ed7c735195 by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] [CUDA] Warm up command buffers that contain convolutions

With CONVOLUTION in command buffers, a convolution's first execution is
recorded inside a stream capture and sets up the DNN library there: the
DNN handle, the runner and, on CUDA, the cuDNN execution plan. That
setup fails inside a capture. Make ConvolutionThunk require a warmup, as
custom calls do, so a command buffer holding a convolution runs once on
each device without recording before it is captured.

--
595ee3a063cfbbefcd7413bc8e3e4541d8efe89e by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] [CUDA] Check requires_warmup of all converted commands

- ConvertConvolutionAndGemmThunks also puts a fusion (KernelThunk) in
  the command buffer.
- Each command's requires_warmup() is checked against a static table
  keyed by Thunk::Kind: copy, kernel and cuBLASLt matmul do not require
  a warmup, convolution does. A command kind missing from the table
  fails the test.

Merging this change closes #52896

head_commit.message:
Re-enable Triton amd-range-analysis lit test and fix overflow patch

The upstream Triton fix (commit 6559dea9d66c20590b4a7aa0cafa850b55269a1e) for
`amd-range-analysis.mlir` has landed, so the test exclusion is no longer needed.
Re-enabling the test exposed a regression in `amd_range_analysis.patch`.
`getTotalLoopTripCount()` clamped trip counts to `kDefaultMaxTripCount + 1`
(1025) instead of only guarding against signed 64-bit overflow.

Use `llvm::MulOverflow` in `getTotalLoopTripCount()` so non-overflowing trip
counts remain exact while overflows fall back to `kDefaultMaxTripCount + 1`.
Remove the test exclusion and regenerate the Triton patch files.

[XLA:GPU] Support native MLIR kInput, multi-output, and DAG stages in MultiPhaseFusion.

`ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` can now lower `kReduction`, `kTranspose`, and `kConcatenate` sub-kernels with any rank, shared memory reuse, partial-CTA barriers, tuple output unpacking, and arbitrary phase DAGs ordered topologically.

display_title: PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

head_commit.message:
PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

When the non-contracting dimension of the left-hand side of a dot consists of two strided segments of a parameter (it's split), we can assign the major segment to be a batch dimension in cuDNN. This only works if there isn't a batch dimension already.

All tensors of the LHS and of the dot itself then must be split in the same way, so that the cuDNN graph has a consistent batch dimension; tensors that are broadcasted along M are left as is.

This is the final change before we can swap out TritonFusionAnalysis from Cudnn Gemm Fusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Align permuted contracting shardings in windowed dot

In `dot_handler.cc`, reduce scatter windowed einsum in `EmitWindowedDotGeneral` and `GetWindowedEinsumConfiguration` gated contracting operand alignment on `RequiresTransposeSharding`, which checks only whether per dimension shard counts differ. When `lhs` and `rhs` have equal contracting shard counts with different device orders across mesh axes, resharding was skipped and partitions contracted mismatched shards. Check `lhs.sharding() != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` when `operands_sharded_at_contracting_dims` is true, and check `lhs_sharding != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` in the cost estimate so permuted contracting shardings reshard before the loop.

display_title: [XLA] Return std::nullopt when Shardy frontend attributes reference a missing mesh

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Return std::nullopt when Shardy frontend attributes reference a missing mesh

After `ShardyXLA` partitions an HLO module, it strips the module-level `xla.sdy.meshes` frontend attribute while parameter and `xla.sdy.FuncResultSharding` instructions can still retain residual `xla.sdy.sharding` frontend attributes referencing `@mesh`. Round-tripping such an HLO module through StableHLO/MHLO and back to HLO previously crashed in `getSdyMeshAttr` (xla/hlo/translate/mhlo_to_hlo/attribute_exporter.cc) with `CHECK(false) << "Mesh not found with name: ..."` when `xla.sdy.meshes` was absent, or dereferenced a null `MeshAttr` if the referenced mesh symbol was missing from `xla.sdy.meshes`.

Return `std::optional<MeshAttr>` from `getSdyMeshAttr` and `std::optional<OpSharding>` from `CreateOpShardingFromSdySharding` so `ExtractShardyArgShardingFromFrontendAttrs` and `ExtractShardyResultShardingFromFrontendAttrs` return `std::nullopt` when a referenced mesh symbol cannot be resolved, while preserving existing conversion behavior for resolved `@mesh` symbols and inlined meshes.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/39824.
Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/47343.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for EighTpu custom call

In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, custom call target `@EighTpu` had no registered `OpShardingRuleAttr` and returned an empty attribute. During Shardy global to local partitioning, `InsertExplicitReshardsPass` skips operations without a sharding rule and `ConvertGlobalToLocalPass` localizes sharded quadrant operands without an `all_gather`, executing independent eigensolvers on disjoint device slices and producing wrong eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Register a sharding rule for validated static square `@EighTpu` calls that propagates leading batch dimensions pointwise and marks the trailing quadrant and eigenvalue dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication`.

head_commit.message:
[PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

`xla::HloSharding` permits tuple shardings and sparse nonnegative explicit
device IDs (`device >= num_devices`), neither of which is valid for
`ifrt::HloShardingSpec` or `ifrt::HloSharding` (where explicit tiled device IDs
index `[0, num_shards)`). In addition, `Unknown` shardings are accepted at
construction, but hit `CHECK` failures instead of returning an error in
`IndexDomains`, `UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

Reject tuple `xla::HloSharding`s and explicit tiled device IDs outside
`[0, num_shards)` in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, and return
`InvalidArgumentError` for `Unknown` shardings in `IndexDomains`,
`UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

head_commit.message:
PR #50727: [CPU] Flush subnormal inputs in the atan2 builtins

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50727

## Summary

XLA:CPU executes libm calls with flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero enabled, and glibc's `atan2`/`atan2f` misbehave on subnormal inputs in that state: subnormal pairs can give the wrong quadrant (for example `atan2(2^-1074, 2^-1074)` returns pi/2 instead of the correct result for flushed inputs), and `atan2f(denorm_min, 1)` can return NaN.

This registers guarded `BuiltinAtan2` and `BuiltinAtan2f` CPU builtins that flush subnormal inputs to signed zero before calling libm. A single templated helper inspects the operand bits (floating-point comparisons can already treat subnormals as zero under DAZ), flushes only nonzero subnormals, and preserves each flushed input's sign so quadrant selection still works. Signed zeros, infinities, and NaNs pass through unchanged. The builtins do not read or modify the floating-point environment, so no denormal state is saved, changed, or restored around the libm call.

Fixes tensorflow/tensorflow#129083.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix and regression tests.

## Tests and validation

- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:builtin_atan2_test`:
  - Hardcoded expectations for flushed f64 and f32 subnormal inputs. Once the inputs are zeroed, every case reduces to one of +/-0, +/-pi/2, or +/-pi.
  - A cross-product loop over subnormal, normal, signed-zero, infinity, and NaN operands under all four FTZ/DAZ state combinations checks that the caller's denormal state is left untouched and that non-subnormal inputs pass through unchanged (compared against `std::atan2`/`atan2f` called directly).
  - `GlibcDenormalMisbehaviors` covers the specific wrong-quadrant and NaN cases seen with glibc.
- `//xla/tests:atan2_test`: new `F64SubnormalOperands` and `F32SubnormalOperands` cases with hardcoded expected results. They use runtime parameters so the subnormal inputs reach compiled code instead of being constant-folded, and they are guarded to CPU only (`test::DeviceTypeIs(test::kCpu)`) because GPU does not zero subnormals and returns pi/4 for `atan2(tiny, tiny)`.
- The issue was reproduced on Linux x86-64 emulation with the reported `tf-nightly==2.23.0.dev20261011`, with the original input bits preserved, and confirmed in a direct libm probe with FTZ/DAZ enabled.
- In this update, `builtin_atan2.cc` was also compiled and run standalone to check the templated helper (flushed pair gives +0, opposite signs give pi, a normal operand against a flushed one gives pi/2, and the f32 case is not NaN). A full local Bazel run of the updated tests was not possible in the current environment (the local Bazel server cannot start), so those results are pending CI.

## Performance

The normal-input path only adds bit inspection of the two operands before the libm call; there is no floating-point state change to pay for. No benchmark numbers are claimed for this version.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Validate and annotate CTA cluster dimensions on LLVM kernels

`AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` previously ignored optional CTA cluster
dimensions on `LaunchDimensions` and did not attach the `"nvvm.cluster_dim"`
LLVM function attribute needed to lower `.reqnctapercluster` in PTX.

Reject cluster dimensions in `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` on non-NVPTX or
pre-Hopper targets, when any coordinate is non-positive, or when `block_counts`
is not divisible by `cluster_dims`. Attach `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` to the kernel
function when `cluster_dims` is set.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass kept the unit dimension of a tt.reduce over a [1, N]
row tile, as the result Triton converted the whole row between layouts through
shared memory. Rewrite such reduces as a 1D reduce plus tt.splat.
This cuts MI350X kernel time by up to 33% (softmax) and 15% (RMSNorm), and
lets 1x32768 tiles with 16 warps compile on MI200/MI300 - avoid error:
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Shared memory size limit exceeded.

head_commit.message:
PR #52609: [ROCm] Port StreamExecutor test cases and fix the gaps they expose

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52609

📝 Summary of Changes
- RocmExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned left start_addr/range_size
  uninitialized when hipDrvPointerGetAttributes does not populate them,
  so the containment check read indeterminate stack values.

- RocmExecutor::GetPointerMemorySpace returned InternalError for
  hipMallocManaged memory. It now queries HIP_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_MANAGED
  first and maps managed/unified memory types to MemorySpace::kUnified

- RocmStream only declared the single-argument DoHostCallbackWithStatus,
  which name-hid the error_cb overload and silently dropped asynchronous
  callback failures. The overload is now implemented, including invoking
  error_cb when the callback cannot be enqueued.

Test cases added:
  - rocm_kernel_test:   ArityZeroKernelSkipsArgumentCountCheck
  - rocm_executor_test: IsHostMemoryPinnedWorksWithRegisteredHostMemory
                      GetPointerMemorySpaceWorksWithUnifiedMemory
  - rocm_stream_test:   DoHostCallbackWithStatusSuccess
                      DoHostCallbackWithStatusError

🎯 Justification
Add more unit test coverage on ROCm platform

🚀 Kind of Contribution:🧪 Tests

display_title: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

head_commit.message:
[XTile][RaggedDot] Let a refused cuDNN probe fall through to another backend

SelectRaggedDotBackend() returned a single choice, so a ragged-dot that
passed the static cuDNN gates but that cuDNN had no execution plan for was
expanded into a dense dot even when the Triton XTile or gpuBLASLt path could
have taken it.

It becomes SelectRaggedDotBackends(), returning the eligible backends in
priority order; an empty result is what RaggedDotRewriter expands, so the
kDefault enumerator is gone.  Callers drop a leading kCuDnn when the cuDNN
probe refuses the ragged-dot and fall through to the next candidate.

RaggedDotRewriter and GemmRewriter must agree on the head of the list, so
GemmRewriter takes the same is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion callback, passed
from AddGemmRewriterPasses.  It only probes when the list holds a candidate
behind kCuDnn: with kCuDnn alone there is nothing to rewrite either way, and
RaggedDotRewriter has already expanded the ragged-dot if cuDNN refused it.
The autotuner pipelines are unchanged; they pass the default cudnn_version,
which keeps kCuDnn out of the list.

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

In `xla/service/cpu/tests/onednn_matmul_test.cc`, enable CPU fast math in `DivisionByConstantWithEltwiseLinearF32` (since oneDNN `LINEAR` post-op fusion relies on `AlgebraicSimplifier` rewriting constant division to multiplication) and add `DivisionByConstantWithoutFastMathNotFusedF32` to verify that division remains unfused when fast math is disabled.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

All tests in `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pass.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Align permuted contracting shardings in windowed dot

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Align permuted contracting shardings in windowed dot

In `dot_handler.cc`, reduce scatter windowed einsum in `EmitWindowedDotGeneral` and `GetWindowedEinsumConfiguration` gated contracting operand alignment on `RequiresTransposeSharding`, which checks only whether per dimension shard counts differ. When `lhs` and `rhs` have equal contracting shard counts with different device orders across mesh axes, resharding was skipped and partitions contracted mismatched shards. Check `lhs.sharding() != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` when `operands_sharded_at_contracting_dims` is true, and check `lhs_sharding != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` in the cost estimate so permuted contracting shardings reshard before the loop.

display_title: Use stable_sort in Triton AllocateWarpGroups and re-enable lit test.

head_commit.message:
Use stable_sort in Triton AllocateWarpGroups and re-enable lit test.

`AllocateWarpGroups` sorted warp-group partitions by descending warp count with unstable `llvm::sort`. When two partitions have equal warp counts, standard library implementations such as libc++ can reorder them. That reordering changes `warpGroupStartIds` and breaks `test/Conversion/allocate_warp_groups.mlir`.

Switch to `llvm::stable_sort` so equal-sized partitions keep their original relative order, and re-enable `Conversion/allocate_warp_groups.mlir`.

display_title: PR #50727: [CPU] Flush subnormal inputs in the atan2 builtins

head_commit.message:
PR #50727: [CPU] Flush subnormal inputs in the atan2 builtins

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50727

## Summary

XLA:CPU executes libm calls with flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero enabled, and glibc's `atan2`/`atan2f` misbehave on subnormal inputs in that state: subnormal pairs can give the wrong quadrant (for example `atan2(2^-1074, 2^-1074)` returns pi/2 instead of the correct result for flushed inputs), and `atan2f(denorm_min, 1)` can return NaN.

This registers guarded `BuiltinAtan2` and `BuiltinAtan2f` CPU builtins that flush subnormal inputs to signed zero before calling libm. A single templated helper inspects the operand bits (floating-point comparisons can already treat subnormals as zero under DAZ), flushes only nonzero subnormals, and preserves each flushed input's sign so quadrant selection still works. Signed zeros, infinities, and NaNs pass through unchanged. The builtins do not read or modify the floating-point environment, so no denormal state is saved, changed, or restored around the libm call.

Fixes tensorflow/tensorflow#129083.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix and regression tests.

## Tests and validation

- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:builtin_atan2_test`:
  - Hardcoded expectations for flushed f64 and f32 subnormal inputs. Once the inputs are zeroed, every case reduces to one of +/-0, +/-pi/2, or +/-pi.
  - A cross-product loop over subnormal, normal, signed-zero, infinity, and NaN operands under all four FTZ/DAZ state combinations checks that the caller's denormal state is left untouched and that non-subnormal inputs pass through unchanged (compared against `std::atan2`/`atan2f` called directly).
  - `GlibcDenormalMisbehaviors` covers the specific wrong-quadrant and NaN cases seen with glibc.
- `//xla/tests:atan2_test`: new `F64SubnormalOperands` and `F32SubnormalOperands` cases with hardcoded expected results. They use runtime parameters so the subnormal inputs reach compiled code instead of being constant-folded, and they are guarded to CPU only (`test::DeviceTypeIs(test::kCpu)`) because GPU does not zero subnormals and returns pi/4 for `atan2(tiny, tiny)`.
- The issue was reproduced on Linux x86-64 emulation with the reported `tf-nightly==2.23.0.dev20261011`, with the original input bits preserved, and confirmed in a direct libm probe with FTZ/DAZ enabled.
- In this update, `builtin_atan2.cc` was also compiled and run standalone to check the templated helper (flushed pair gives +0, opposite signs give pi, a normal operand against a flushed one gives pi/2, and the f32 case is not NaN). A full local Bazel run of the updated tests was not possible in the current environment (the local Bazel server cannot start), so those results are pending CI.

## Performance

The normal-input path only adds bit inspection of the two operands before the libm call; there is no floating-point state change to pay for. No benchmark numbers are claimed for this version.
