display_title: PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

head_commit.message:
PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49580

📝 Summary of Changes
#ai_generated (but it's been in use internally for several weeks)

When XLA:CPU reduces a large array, it first splits the reduction into a reduce-window that produces partial sums and a smaller reduce over those. The fusion pass knows how to *fuse producers into a reduce*, but not into a *reduce-window*. So in something like `sum(x * y)`, the multiply generates its own loop and writes its entire result to memory, which is read immediately after by the reduce (instead of performing a more optimal loop fusion).

The actual fix is adding `kReduceWindow` to `CanBeLoopFused`, which is one line. I also had to teach `ReusesOperandElements` that a reduce-window with non-overlapping windows touches each input element only once, *as is already done for reduce*.

🎯 Justification

This affects every large reduction that doesn't go to YNNPACK. I ran into it while looking into #49131.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

```
ENTRY main {
  x = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(0)
  y = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(1)
  m = bf16[64,1048576] multiply(x, y)
  c = bf16[] constant(0)
  ROOT r = bf16[64] reduce(m, c), dimensions={1}, to_apply=add
}
```

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| bf16 (above) | 78.0 ms | 28.8 ms |
| same in s32 | 77.7 ms | 12.7 ms |

I didn't see any changes outside the noise on the other CPU benchmarks.

🧪 Unit Tests:

New tests in `hlo_instruction_test` check that a reduce-window reuses elements only when its windows overlap. In `cpu_instruction_fusion_test`, one test fuses a multiply into a non-overlapping reduce-window and another checks that `exp` stays out of an overlapping one.

There was also an existing test in `cpu_fusion_test` that used reduce-window as its example of an op that can't be fused, which is no longer true, so I switched it to sort.
Copybara import of the project:

--
1557a803471eab5d9fe3a3b9b2788b259150452b by jurasic <jurasic@proximafusion.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

TreeReductionRewriter splits large reductions into a reduce-window followed by
a reduce. CPU fusion did not accept kReduceWindow, so the input of the
reduce-window was always materialized.

Allow fusing producers into a reduce-window if its windows do not overlap and
are not dilated, so every input element is read once. A reduce-window is never
fused into its consumer. Make ReusesOperandElements return false for the array
operands of such a reduce-window, as it already does for kReduce. Also treat a
max reduce-window like a max reduce when looking for the softmax shift pattern.

Merging this change closes #49580

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

Pipelined dot mainloops previously did not account for shared-memory bandwidth.
When a >=32-bit dot operand cannot vectorize async global-to-shared loads along
its minor dimension (due to a non-unit tile stride or odd dimension size) and
its padded minor tile size does not exceed the thread count, Triton uses an
unswizzled transposed shared-memory layout that suffers bank conflicts.

Bounding multi-stage, multi-iteration K-loops by SM shared-memory throughput
(including bank-conflict serialization) ensures the cost model does not
underprice pipelined tiles bottlenecked on shared memory.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024750426

display_title: PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.
Copybara import of the project:

[XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

A call annotated with _xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>" is
wrapped into an async region by ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper and
assigned LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>) by ExecutionStreamAssignment, so it
runs on that domain's stream. The wrapper rejects locality-domain regions
that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and
AsyncStartThunk::Prepare rejects communication thunks inside them at
runtime. Stream annotations are kept only on the call, not on the
get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.

Merging this change closes #52821

`CollectiveMemory::FindWeakSymmetricMemory` now returns the byte offset of the allocation inside the symmetric window instead of always 0. `CollectiveKernelThunk` remembers that offset next to the cached window and rebuilds its peer pointer table when it changes. The ragged all-to-all bounds check validates writes against both the destination buffer slice and the symmetric window.

Today every window is registered for exactly one allocation, so the offset is always 0 and behavior does not change. This prepares for registering one window for a whole collective memory arena, where buffers live at non-zero offsets inside the window.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

The PJRT GPU client now adds a sub-allocator free visitor that calls `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory`, next to the existing allocator memory registration visitors, and passes the free visitors to every collective memory allocator: the separate collective BFC allocator (through a new `CreateCollectiveBFCAllocator` parameter) and the "platform" `StreamExecutorMemoryAllocator`, in addition to the BFC and VMM allocators that already received them.

This makes sure a symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator never outlives the device allocation it was registered for. Until registrations are actually cached on communicators the visitor finds nothing to release. One cost is that the "platform" allocator now synchronizes the device before freeing a collective buffer, because it has a free visitor; a later change only installs the visitor when caching on communicators is enabled.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model dot shared-memory pipe throughput and cp.async bank conflicts.

Pipelined dot mainloops previously did not account for shared-memory bandwidth.
When a >=32-bit dot operand cannot vectorize async global-to-shared loads along
its minor dimension (due to a non-unit tile stride or odd dimension size) and
its padded minor tile size does not exceed the thread count, Triton uses an
unswizzled transposed shared-memory layout that suffers bank conflicts.

Bounding multi-stage, multi-iteration K-loops by SM shared-memory throughput
(including bank-conflict serialization) ensures the cost model does not
underprice pipelined tiles bottlenecked on shared memory.

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

Unchunked `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()` plans in `xla/pjrt/transpose.cc` previously used a 1 MiB (`1 << 20`) per-thread parallelization threshold while non-memcpy transpose plans used 64 MiB (`1 << 26`). When memory-bandwidth-bound 1-D or tiled contiguous copies larger than 1 MiB run via `TransposePlan` alongside concurrent async transfers, fanning each copy out across up to 16 threads adds host CPU contention and thread overhead without reducing aggregate H2D wall time.

Unify `kMinBytesPerThread` for `chunk_contiguity_ == ChunkContiguity::kNone` to 64 MiB (`1 << 26`) regardless of `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()`, matching non-memcpy transpose plans and the 64 MiB `kFastPathMaxBytes` threshold in `xla/pjrt/tiled_linearizer.cc`. Plans with contiguous chunking (`ChunkContiguity::kOutput` / `ChunkContiguity::kInput`) keep `kMinBytesPerThread = 1` so chunked pipelined transfers remain parallelized below 64 MiB.

Testing:
* Added `TransposeTest.MemcpyParallelizationThreshold` in `xla/pjrt/transpose_test.cc` covering 16 MiB, 64 MiB, and 128 MiB 1-D copies (`kNone`) and 16 MiB 2-D tiled copies (`kNone` vs `kOutput`).
* Ran `//xla/pjrt:transpose_test` (all shards pass).
* In a 51-step A/B profile of concurrent async H2D transfers on a multi-host TPU training workload, this cut host thread-summed `Transpose::ExecuteChunk` time by 33% (224.9 → 150.0 ms/step), cut host thread count in the trace by 35% (642 → 416), and kept H2D wall-clock union span flat (13.38 → 13.27 ms/step).
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024700757

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the parent keeps the child-handle storage alive until it is torn down. `PollUntilDone` now reports a failed `ncclCommGetAsyncError` query separately from an async operation error.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.
Copybara import of the project:

16ca7fc76dcb82c380e800cad86aaf902849ecac by Jane Liu <janeliu@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add clique-level release of cached symmetric memory.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add clique-level release of cached symmetric memory.

Adds `ReleaseSymmetricMemory(device_id, addr)` to `GpuClique`, `LockableGpuClique` and a process-wide `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory` in `gpu_cliques.h`. It forwards the release to every communicator of every live clique that runs on the given local device.

When a collective memory buffer is freed, any symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator for that buffer must be dropped, otherwise a later allocation at the same address would reuse a stale window. The allocator does not know which cliques use the buffer, so the release goes to all cliques on the device. Cliques are tracked for this in a separate registry of weak pointers with its own mutex, because the release will run on allocator free paths and must not wait for the process clique mutex, which can be held for a whole run while a clique is abandoned. No callers yet.

display_title: [XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

📝 Summary of Changes

HloRematerialization's host-offload strategy picks a candidate from the buffer-level user list (GetUsers, every position of the value), but OffloadInstruction places the copy back to device before the first unplaced user in the instruction's own users(). The two lists differ when the value is also read through another instruction's output, for example forwarded into an async-start's output tuple and read by the async-done. If the only direct user (the async-start) is already placed, OffloadInstruction finds nothing and CHECK-fails: "Have nothing to place this before!".

GetCostOfHostOffload now rejects candidates whose buffer has indirect uses. This is conservative: OffloadInstruction only rewires direct users, and the memory tracker would hand the indirect users to the new copy and count the original buffer as free while a placed async-start still holds it. ExtendRecomputeBlock already skips such buffers for recompute because liveness is hard to reason about.

Compression is not changed. It cannot hit this CHECK (it needs an unplaced direct user), but AddCompressInstructions has the same accounting problem when a placed async-start coexists with an unplaced direct user. That deserves its own change and test.

🎯 Justification

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51432. The module from the issue aborts GPU compilation at head (hlo-opt --platform=gpu --stage=hlo-backend, a100_sxm_80 target spec, --xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading=true). With this change it compiles.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in hlo_rematerialization_test.cc. SkipOffloadWhenOnlyUserIsAsyncStart: the only user of an add is an already placed async-start; without the fix it aborts on the CHECK. SkipOffloadWhenAsyncStartIsPlacedBeforeDirectUser: the add also has a later direct user; without the fix it is offloaded anyway and the tracker reports a 4 KiB saving while the async-start still holds the buffer. With the fix both leave the add alone and offload the next candidate.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

display_title: PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

head_commit.message:
PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation. The runtime version is necessary but not sufficient — the kernel driver, the container or the device may still refuse fd export — so a rejected granularity query or hipMemCreate() falls back to hipMemHandleTypeNone with a warning, as the CUDA allocator does. Workloads that never export keep running.

🎯 Justification

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: ✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests: Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both directions, the fallback leaving allocation intact, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer from the kVmm allocator.

Copybara import of the project:

display_title: Honor --xla_dump_hlo_module_re and --xla_enable_dumping in ShardyXLA.

head_commit.message:
Honor --xla_dump_hlo_module_re and --xla_enable_dumping in ShardyXLA.

Previously, `ShardyXLA`'s MLIR dump directory check only inspected `--xla_dump_to` and `--xla_dump_hlo_pass_re`, dumping every compiled module whenever the pass filter matched (or contained `shardy-verbose`) even when `--xla_dump_hlo_module_re` restricted dumping to specific modules or `--xla_enable_dumping` was false.

Check `xla_enable_dumping()` and `DumpingEnabledForHloModule()` before enabling Shardy MLIR dumps or `shardy-verbose` propagation debug tracking, and guard against unset `TEST_UNDECLARED_OUTPUTS_DIR` when `--xla_dump_to=sponge`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support dots with downstream transposes in indexing cost model.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support dots with downstream transposes in indexing cost model.

Move the downstream `kTranspose` rejection out of
`gpu_dot_fusion_cost_model::IsSupported` into
`EstimateRunTimeForDotOpWithBlockParameters` so `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`
can model dot fusions with transposed outputs using the tile sizes already
propagated backward to the `dot` instruction. Also scale dot-operand L2 reads
by 32-byte sector utilization so strided gathers pay for whole L2 sectors, and
scale dot compute when reshaped output tilings launch more threadblocks than
the dot's own tile grid.
